title: Harry Potter Tour of Warner Bros. Studio with Transport from London
description: Located on the outskirts of London, Warner Bros. Studio is home to a treasure trove of Harry Potter film sets, costumes, props, and other special mementos. On this tour, climb aboard a comfortable coach at a time of your choosing and head straight there. You have time to independently explore the exhibits, take photos, browse the gift shop, and even enjoy a glass of butterbeer (at your own expense).

reviews.usertext: The best day ever! My son and I booked a while ago to go to Harry Potter World and have been looking forward to it ever since-and we weren't disappointed. Our 9am time slot made it an early start but it was well worth it. From the moment we arrived we said 'wow' and every turn we made this continued throughout the entire tour. The staff were amazing too and brought the tour to life with their enthusiasm. Our favourite parts were Diagon Alley and the Hogwarts Express. Be prepared to spend extra money on photos etc as there are 2 green screen areas and who can resist buying a photo of their child flying on a broomstick past Hogwarts? However, there are other free activities such as wand training which you are allowed to video. We took our lunch with us and as it was a nice day sat outside as there is only two food areas, one at the start and one halfway through the tour which gets very busy at lunchtime. Lots of clean toilets dotted throughout. Take a decent camera as we took loads of photos and videos. The gift shop is mind-blowing but be careful as some products are not priced up, but something for all price ranges. We didn't use the shuttle bus from Watford Junction but this runs every 20mins. We got dropped off and picked up by a relative right outside main entrance no problems. We didn't use the digital guide as videos and info boards telling you about the sets as you go round. It was a magical experience we won't forget in a hurry.

We absolutely loved it! We had been here before, around five years ago, but there are loads of new things to see.

The cost of the food is what you expect it to be (not cheap). It cost us £45 for four meals. The butterbeer is £7 each but you’ve got to keep the plastic tumbler which makes a nice souvenir.

The only thing I didn’t like was that you can’t go into the shop before the tour. So if you want to purchase a wand or a costume to wear you can’t do this. There is a small shop on platform 9 3/4 with a limited range, but by that time you already halfway round.

Book well ahead and take lots of money with you! We didn’t go mad but with lunch and butterbeer for four people, a couple of souvenirs and some photos we spent in excess of £200.

Despite that we will still go back!

From the moment we arrived at the Warner Brother Studio Tour everything felt very safe. The que to get in was short and managed by pre booking your time slot. Bag searches, compulsory mask wearing and temperature checks made everyone feel safe as you entered the building.

Once inside WOW! This is the second time I have visited here and it is safe to say they keep on improving. The train, Gringotts, Forbidden Forest and the large dragon were all new since my last visit and they were incredible. I loved the entrance video and the staff were ever so helpful and friendly. Seeing the sets and props that they used in the films is amazing and it makes you feel like you are right in the action of the films. It was nice to see the touch areas like barriers were constantly sanitized by staff too. There were also ample hand sanitising stations around the attraction.

A couple of times it felt a little bit manic and busy inside and some people did keep taking their masks off for photos which was a bit frustrating when they asked for masks on. The gift shop was a very impressive size and had lots of merchandise to choose from, but was incredibly expensive. I think you need to rob Gringotts on the way around to afford things!

Overall a very enjoyable 3-4 hour trip around the studio tour. I will definitely recommend it to friends and family as a fantastic day out.

Was mixed up on arrival date and missed the tour by a day after paying $379.13 dollars. The company was not sympathetic and did not credit, or give any options for a rebook. I realize this was my fault about the day, but do not understand why they would not help with crediting toward another day.

I struggled with loosing this money for a few days, looking for any option of recovering it, or getting some sort of credit. There isn't a way. If you miss your time slot, you will loose all money.

What I would recommend to anybody thinking about going to Harry Potter is to buy the tickets from the studio directly. Trip advisor will not let me add the link, but, you can find the web site by finding the location of the studio on google maps, then hit the website button. It is much cheaper, for me it would have been 200 dollars cheaper for 2 adults and 1 child. You will though need to work out transportation to the studio. Use the underground and public transportation. Once you start using it, it is quite easy.

Good luck!

The Warner Brothers Studio and experience was fantastic. Really great seeing the magic of the making the Harry Potter movies. The bus ride to and from the studios was not great, however. Instead of being immersed in Harry Potter with music, trivia, or tales of the making, we were immersed in loud Latin music and a blasting heater. The driver couldn’t hear us asking to turn down the heat because the music was so loud. For the price of this excursion, I expected to be in the Harry Potter world from the get go. The studio tickets are only 50 pounds, so we paid $200 a person to hear Latin music in London in 90 degree bus. Definitely not worth the money.

A great day out for my daughters 10 th birthday spoiled by the first staff member we encountered (Eddie) at the entrance swearing (F*** words) to his fellow security team members. He didn’t even stop despite our children being present and my shocked stare at him. I completed a complaint form at the reception and was told this was exactly a scenario they had trained for. I received a quick apology from the receptionist and that was it. I haven’t received any other contact which I am a bit disappointed by as I left my contact information.

The museum was great but the queue for the butter beer was about 30 minutes which we found excessive for drinks only

Fantastic place but ruined by rude foul mouthed security staff and long queues in the cafe

If you LOVE the Harry Potter franchise then this is for you. If you only have limited time in London, then really consider whether this is time well spent with your family. It is not in Central London. Costly to get to and costly to get in. We trained from Euston to Watford Junction, then you have to pay for a shuttle bus that takes you to the studio. The timed tickets are meaningless as they really don’t check time and you can start whenever you get there. At the start you are taken to a room where there is a film of people talking about how they love Harry Potter. Then you are taken to a theatre for a short film about making of Harry Potter. Then you start the walking self guided tour. It is like walking in a museum of Harry Potter props and scenes from filming set. It is quite a lot of walking as you are basically walking on 2 sound stages. There is butter beer for purchase but at a price of £6.95 for a soft drink with souvenir mug.

Overall, not value for money.

Amazing setting for all ages and well worth it

We attended as a family having booked the tickets months ago. The studios are accessible from all areas of London and if you travel by train upon arrival at Watford Junction, there is a Harry Potter Studio bus which is £3 return and takes you to the studio. You don't need to book this, just go to the buses and a member of staff will check your tickets.
Arriving at the studio the service was excellent, especially during current covid times. Social distancing is adhered even through the first part of the tour.
We purchased the digital guide, if I was going again I would say you wouldn't need this as it's clearly sign posted.
You can fly the magic wand, even as an adult i did this and you can purchase the photos or USB at the end.
The staff were all very helpful and wore masks at all times, the majority of the public did too!
The only small negative is the cost of food and drink it's really expensive.
Overall this is a must and we all thoroughly enjoyed it

This tour is out of this World; it is in the Wizarding World. It’s long. You’re walking around for about 3 1/2 to 4hrs. BUT you are visiting the actual sets used in the films. Think about this. Alan Rickman, Richard Harris, Michael Gambon, Daniel Radcliffe, Rupert Grint, Emma Watson all used these sets to bring us into J K Rowling’s magical world and we now get to walk in their very footsteps.

The staff were wonderful and very knowledgeable. Ask anything and they know the answer; like why did Professor Flitwick (actor Warwick Davies) change appearance during the series? Who stole the number plate on number 4 Privet Drive? That’s actually on display if you look for it.

Many of the costumes are on display as well as loads of memorabilia. For budding photographers out there yet to go, you won’t need your flash. The lighting team have been in during lockdown, and re-lit EVERY scene (except the portrait of Salazar Slytherin) so that pretty much every digital camera will get a perfect shot every time.

Have a wonderful day in this magical world, and discover even more magic when you get home! Your wallet or bank account is empty or your credit card is maxed out. BEWARE the gift shop. The prices here are steeper than the top slopes of Everest, and higher than its peak.

I don’t know who set the prices, but after getting in, being fed and watered, and being asked for astronomical prices in the gift shop, Warner Bros better not complain of low revenue in their U.K. division.
Now I’m off to sit under a fan in this heatwave and enjoy a butterbeer. Cheers!

We had a nice bus ride to the Making of Harry Potter. The only tour involved was the audio tour at the Harry Potter studio (costs 10 pounds per person and not included in this purchase). It was purely our bus driver transporting us to the WB Studio location and nothing more. I used the time to nap from such a long flight, so this made for a great arrival day adventure to start. I’d recommend for those running this business to consider stepping up the trip’s excitement with a guide or driver who might discuss HP and what to watch out for at the studios.

For purposes of this review the poor rating applies only to the premium bus company. I would not classify them as a tour company. They simply dropped us at Harry Potter and delivered us back. There was no conversation on the bus. The bus smelled like urine and was filthy. Harry Potter Studio Tour was fantastic. Find a different way to get there!

This was incredible. It is done extremely well. There are lots of things to look at ,read about and try out.
You wait in a room prior to going into the grand Hall, there is a bit of backstory talking which younger children aren't interested in. But after that it was v good.

Prior to coming I paid for the audio tour guide packs for our family. Unless you are fascinated about the details of making a movie etc then you don't need this. My children really like Harry Potter but weren't at all interested in their audio tour and gave up quite quickly. There were others, mostly young adults who were using theirs.

For a family day out you don't need them.

The staff were helpful and polite.
The shop is quite overwhelming at the end, so be warned those with children, it is a large area and full of items they will 'need'. The queue in the shop to pay took a long time but it was v busy.

The buses to and from Watford Junction worked extremely well and were on time, no waiting and the driver polite.

This was a great trip overall.

The Harry Potter Studio tour was fantastic. Very entertaining and informative — mind blowing how much work goes into the production of these movies. Our lunches were good and reasonably priced, especially considering you have no where else to eat! I had the chicken pie and my husband had the beef. I subtract one star for the “Premium Tour” transportation. It was on time and the coach was clean, but It wasn’t clear where to meet at the Victoria Coach Station. We were called because we were late checking in (it was 9:20) and told which platform to go to or we may have missed the bus! There isn’t really any tour — no information — just silence and then “we are here, here’s your ticket, get off the bus and be back here before 3:00.” I don’t know how difficult it is to get tickets and arrange your own transportation, but I question whether it’s really worth the premium. Pun intended. That said, it was the perfect amount of time at the studio and we had great fun.

If you’re contemplating this tour, think no further and just do it! It is absolutely worth the money. A quick bus ride from London to the studios, and the magic begins. Seeing the filming locations from our favorite films was extraordinary. We loved the multiple opportunities for photos, especially being able to ride a Nimbus 2000 in a quidditch match.

The only reason I did not leave a five star review was because of the bus experience. The bus itself was nice, however finding the departure area was difficult. We were told to go to Victoria Station, but not told where to meet the driver. After waiting in the ticket line, we found the driver (Ben) who proceeded to yell at us because he said he was “yelling our name”. We had arrived 15 minutes early as instructed, yet there was no signs indicating where to meet. Ben, the driver, completely berated our friend when she explained that we were lost. At one point she looked at us in surprise, and he told her “don’t look at them, look at me!” It wasn’t the best start to the day. At the end of the trip, we waited on the bus for the other passengers. We were to leave the studios at 5; it was 5:13 and he announced that we had 6 passengers who were not on the bus, so he was going to leave them. I was shocked. When he finally dropped us all off at the station, he actually sat with his hand out waiting for a tip….he of course received not one!!!

Overall, we didn’t let Ben ruin our trip. It was an incredible experience that I highly recommend to others!!!

We booked with City Wonders and Ticmate. The overall experience was great. Could have given it a 5 if there were more options for the food to buy at the studio during the break. The tour guides were knowlegeable and great at their jobs. We were met by one guide (dressed like a witch with a soeting hat😄) at the Euston War Memorial outside Euston station and accompanied us from the train to Waterford Junction, where we took the bus going to Warner Bros Studios. We were then turned over to the other tour guide who showed us around, gave us some extra information and some trivia about actors and scenes. The butter beer is not as good as the one in Orlando Universal Studios though, but still ok.

This was a great tour not to be missed for Harry Potter fans. I would say the premium small group tour is outstanding (that is what we did) but it is expensive. For a die hard HP fan, though, it is worth it. The premium tour is done by a cast member at the same time as the regular tour with a limit of 8 guests. The total value of the tour is made up with photo and video components. The lunch is nice but is typical pub fare. The real key is that you complete the tour in two hours, have a meal and then have the rest of the day to go back and go through the studio again on your own. The second time was just as good as the first as we were able to see a lot of the “Easter eggs” in person after they had been shown. They also had good shopping experiences and the butter beer was good as well.

For the HP fan that is not a super fan - I think the regular tour which is a lower price would probably be fine. For the super fan - the premium tour is probably going to be considered superior even with the price difference.

Transportation wise, we took the train to Watford Junction and then the bus to the studio campus - travel was easy to accomplish. Cost of transit was about 16 pounds per person if that helps people decide. Trains are plentiful and easy to do. bus to and from the campus is 3 pounds.

This tour is heavenly overpriced and a disappointing experience due to bad management of the trip. The visit to the Warner Bros. Studios is recommended and fun, but the tour with the bus is not. First we missed the bus at the starting point. Nowhere is mentioned that you should go inside the bus station building and find a gate where the bus is staying. Second, staff at the site pointed us to another place across the street where other busses stood. Third, when we called the organisation (3 times) nobody picked up and so we missed the bus and had to take a taxi ourselves to the location. On the way back we made it to the bus, but the driver was very unfriendly, missed two passengers at the studios who were a bit too late and he also did not give way to passengers on crossings. All in all you can better take a taxi to the location and back which is only 40 pounds one-way and cheaper than this whole tour including the entrance ticket.

I booked this tour very last minute when I couldnt get ticket direct for the studios, while it is expensive in comparison to making your own way there, I was sending my mother in law who walks with an aid and my 9 year old so was given peace of mind they get dropped off there etc. This is a stress free option in my opinion for first time visitors.
Before the tour I needed to call premium tours for some help they were really helpful, i spoke to a lady on the phone unsure of her name but she explained everything to me.
The coach was easy to find and very clean and comfy.
My mother in law was very looked after they asked if she needed extra help etc.
They absolutely LOVED the studio and had more than enough time to walk round even with them taking it slowly and stopping for lunch.
Would definitely recommend for anyone unsure of getting trains, driving there as is quite far from central london. The staff were great and overall i was happy with the price i paid.

Visited here as a family of three with our 9 year daughter.
Easy to book online and chose the option of an e-ticket so no queue.
Ample parking and you can pay extra (£10) to get a space close to the entrance. Lots of staff to guide you to the right area.

Considering it was half term the queues were very minimal and the staff managed the flow really well.
We all had a really lovely time and have some great pictures. Our favourites were the Grongotts Bank, the Night Bus and Diagon Alley. I won’t say anymore as I don’t want to ruin any surprises!
It’s a must for all Harry Potter fans.
The only thing that spoilt it for us was having to wear a mask the entire time.

We ate once we finished the tour so am unable to comment on the food in the cafe half way round.
The food was amazing and they catered for me (no wheat/gluten) which was an added bonus!
My daughter had a pizza, we had burger and chips and were all impressed with the quality.
We had an ice cream for pudding, rather pricey at £6 for a cone and £9 for a sharing cup. The sharing cup would have been ample for all three of us but never mind. The ice cream was also amazing!
They could do with some more low/no sugar drinks for the kids.

All in all we had a great time and highly recommend visiting.

I know that giving money to JK Rowling is a terrible thing. We booked this in 2019, were given credit and rebooked twice since. While I did think that JK Rowling wasn’t a great human back then, it has become glaringly obvious since I originally booked the tickets that she’s a raging transphobe. It still makes me uncomfortable, but on the flip side, this event isn’t for me, my daughters special interest for years was Harry Potter, and I always promised her that I would take her. So we went. It doesn’t feel ethically good, but the smile on her face lit up the whole room (surprisingly Mace loved it too), so I’m going to quietly sit with my bad feelings about JK and let my kids live their Harry Potter fantasy…
This was good, really good. They suggest leaving 4 hours for it, and by the time we got merch, it was just short of 4.5 hours, plus an hour or more (almost two is there is a National rail and tube strike) each way and it’s a pretty solid day. It’s worth it, I don’t want to say it, but it was very special, particularly if you have/had a Harry Potter obsession. So much to see, the food has catered for vegans and GF! We had a great day, but that will be the last of mine and JKs time together.

My husband, teenagers and I absolutely loved our trip here. If you love Harry Potter like us (especially the movies) this is a must do. I will admit that it is pretty pricey though. The tickets themselves, the photos/videos, the food and everything in the gift shop is expensive. But it is somewhat worth your money, you could spend a whole day here and still not see everything. Almost anything that you could think of from the movies you can see here. For big Harry Potter fans it’s worth your time and money to come here.

Obviously, it's cheaper to get to the studios using public transit. I decided it was worth the extra 30 pounds or so to travel with Premium Tours, and I'm glad I did. Pickup was easy at Victoria COACH Station (not Victoria Station). They were at gate 0 for me. It's only about 75 minute drive (or less) each way, so you get plenty of time at the studios (which are totally amazing!). I took the 9:15 tour and the studios weren't too crowded, but shortly thereafter they became truly packed, so I wouldn't recommend going much later. This was on a Wednesday, by the way.

Dropoff is at Victoria station, which was great for tube access. Saved a ton of time and the hassle of public transit getting to the studios! I'd recommend Premium Tours.

Interactive and wonderful experience for any Harry Potter Fan. We went (2 teens, 1 -11 y/o) and had a great time. Would highly recommend even if you were not a super fan of the HP series. There is much to see and interactive with getting passport stamps. There is a cafeteria for lunch. Butterbeer was disappointing compared to what we had at Universal Studios, CA. The store was great. We enjoyed our experience. We took the tourbus from near Westminister area and it took us to the studio. We had originally planned to take the train but b/c of rail strikes we booked the Golden Tours bus. I will say, if you get motion sick do not ride at the top of the bus. Sit on the bottom level. Except for my motion sickness, we all enjoyed the WB HP tour and would recommend.

We used Premium tour as a way to access the Harry Potter Studio. At first we thought that it was just going to be a boring ride on a bus that you would want to finish as quick as you could. Nevertheless, we had the pleasure to land on Malcolm, a great/funny/kind guy who gave us lots informations about London: I admit that I, in reality, didn't want our ride to end. He made lots of joke and made everyone feel comfortable in his bus.
We 100% recommend this company and advise you to pray that you land on Malcom because he is the best!
Thanks again!!!

The sets are very interesting, more so if you get the self guided tour. You need 3-4 hours to do the sets justice. The cafe is half way through the exhibition with burgers and hot dogs and of course, it wraps at the gift shop.

Very good but v pricey and can’t use cash in food hall which is annoying when you’ve saved cash to take. Plus mask still required when law has ended requiring them indoors which for 3 hours makes it v uncomfortable. The tour itself is brilliant. Vv expensive for photos etc which naturally the children want taking. Then the shop. Omg take a bank loan. A small choc wand £5. Prob less choc than a £1 Cadbury bar. Again frustrating when children have taken their money and even small things were v pricey. The Christmas shop especially was v v pricey

This was a wonderful inside look into the studios and the making of the films. The sets were amazing and made you feel like you were there. It was a bit crowded with multiple tour groups coming through at the same time but I guess that attests to the evergreen popularity of the Harry Potter franchise! If you book the tour that leaves from Victoria Coach Station, just bring your voucher to the gate. You’ll get your tickets after you board the bus (the instructions were a bit confusing and many of us thought we had to get our tickets before getting on the bus). Our bus driver was very entertaining! It was a fun experience!

Value for money! It was an experience I would never forget and I would highly recommend. The trip from London to the studios was on time. And once you get to the studios, you will be impressed by the whole production and set-up that makes you appreciate the tour even more. There is nothing like it!

This was a dream come true. The studio tour is something HP fans should not miss, but it also has a lot to offer to people who are not really fans. The installations are amazing and interesting and the fact that the movies were actually shot here is just magical.

As I’m visiting London from the states, transportation to the studio was a concern and Premium Tours solved all of my problems! The Victoria Station pickup was at a reasonable time and easily accessible. Our bus driver, Malcom, was an absolute delight and kept our group entertained on the drive out to the studio. The tour itself is a must-see experience for any Harry Potter fans. I am beyond glad that I booked this experience through Premium Tours!

We travelled for our daughters birthday and was not disappointed. Just expect it to be very very busy and 1hr queue to get food there. The food is very expensive with the Butter Beer being £6:95 for a small mug (you could keep that). Take your own picnic. The guides on the tour are good but the canteen staff are very rude and obnoxious. Please please please do not stay at the Double Tree Hilton (Boreham Wood) if booking a package. It is shockingly bad. You have been warned.

This was an amazing visit, all of my 3 teens and 2 adults loved this place. It's magical, to say the least and set is most definitely awe inspiring and makes you feel like it is real. A bit ways to get out there on your own, like I did, not too hard. Took a train and then jumped on the bus that took us to the studio.

Will do this again.

Fantastic - even for a muggle this place is jaw dropping. This was our third visit and we will be back before the year is out . You can actually do this trip yourself by public transport from Waterloo to Watford Junction and then there is a free shuttle coach to the studios and it will end up costing you a fraction of the price. Just to say I have not used this service so I am not reviewing the service given by Premium tours .A family ticket cost €132 for 2 adults and 2 children and then the extras are just the train fare. If you are on a budget I would recommend exploring this option.

My son and I visited The Warner Brothers Harry Potter Studio Tour in London in February for my 60th birthday celebration. We had an amazing time at the Harry Potter Studio Tour. The layout was amazing, standing in Dumbledore’s office was thrilling, seeing Hagrid’s hut was very cool, and the staff rounded off the experience with extra trivia as well as their own excitement of working there. The woman working by Dumbledore’s office when we were there on February 11, was nice as pie, told us extra trivia bits and told us how much she wants to visit Canada. A true angel. And a female staff member took our photo in front of the castle. Also, Keith, a security guard who ended our day with lovely tales about the studio was absolutely marvellous. My son and I still talk about how kind and helpful he was. Thank you to all the staff. Visiting the studio was a real highlight of our trip.

If you are not a serious Harry Potter fan, save your money. The serious fan in our group liked most of this tour but felt some of the “magic” was spoiled by seeing the behind the scenes. The rest of the group were not interested and felt that it was overpriced and not worth the expense. If you are not a serious fan, save your money

We had a fantastic day as I’m sure is to be pretty much expected if you’re a Harry Potter fan, but what we had not expected was the fantastic customer service for our son with autism.
When we showed our tickets, the lady said she’d noticed our son wearing a sunflower lanyard as asked if there was anything she could help with to make our visit easier. She offered us a fidget toy and ear defenders. She told us there was a quiet space if we needed it. She also quietly told us about a couple of parts we may need to be prepared for, without our children hearing so no parts were spoilt.
We accepted the fidget toy which really helped when queuing. We didn’t think we’d need the ear defenders but she said we could ask anyone for some at any time.
We really felt like our visit was going to be successful even before we’d entered and that’s half the battle on days out.
We didn’t spot it before we went but there is a really helpful social story on the website which can be used to prepare a child.
Thank you Warner Bros for your autism awareness and training. It does make a difference

This isn’t a review of the Warner Bros studio experience itself, which is fascinating, but of the so called “tour” provided by Premium. There was nothing wrong with the coach or the driver but paying £100 on top of the standard studio entrance fee for what is essentially just a return bus ride from central London just represents really poor value for money. There is nothing Harry Potter-esque about this; and no survival extras to enhance the experience. Find another way to get to the Studios and save your money!

Amazing place not to be missed by adults a d children alike.
Makes more sense if you have read the books and seen the films.
Only criticism was the cafe. Had to queue for ages. Should have been a separate queue for prepared sandwiches etc.
Part of my family queued for more than 30 minutes while I joined the queue for butter beer and ice cream.
I was done in less than 10 minutes so was standing with melting ice cream.

The prices of everything to to with this are massively over inflated. I can understand the high entry cost to a point, but the total rip off prices in the food outlets and shop are just disgusting.
I cannot understand how they can charge so much for everything, families on lower incomes don't stand a chance here. I'm fortunate that I could afford it, but others cannot. The gift shop is the worst I have ever seen. It must be heartbreaking for children to denied something because their parents can't afford these stupid prices.

My other complaint is with the customer services team who refused to change the visit date for my daughter after her baby became ill the night before they were due to visit. I had paid for their tickets which is another £100 wasted.

Went on the 24th June. Had a fantastic time - staff were lovely, lots to see and do and in the end we spent a good 3 hours here. I would like to mention that Lauren, who was in the Gringotts Section was fantastic - took the time to talk to us about the set, provided some really fun facts and talk about Harry Potter and all things nerdy. She gave superb customer service and I hope she gets recognised for it. All the sets are well displayed and there is a lot of information about the history of the making of the film. The measures the studio has in place for COVID 19 and the restrictions meant we felt safe. Midway through the tour you get a chance to try Butterbeer and Butterbeer Ice Cream - it’s worth doing! Plus you can pay extra for a tankard and cute ice cream bowl. The shop at the end is full of exclusive merchandise that i would’ve easily spent a small fortune in but I had to limit myself. At the moment there is a Slytherin Event which is worth seeing! I can’t wait to book tickets again to see the tour during the Christmas period.

It was our third visit and we always enjoy. The car parking and queue control is good and pleased were enforcing mask wearing there is also plenty of hand sanitising stations. We had visited at Christmas and spring before so we wanted to see it at Halloween, the Great Hall was set up with pumpkins and the death eaters were good. The tour itself is great for all Harry Potter fans and film fans as to see the way things are done is interesting. We spent over 3 hours exploring and enjoyed the butter beer and ice cream in between. We made the mistake of going for afternoon tea at the Mecure hotel, part of our voucher deal, nearby afterwards we wished we had not and had stayed and tried the food at the chocolate frog cafe instead! The shop is expensive and seems to have become even more so. We have enjoyed all our visits and would visit again.

The studios themselves were incredible! So much to see and do (if only they didn't nickel and dime you for everything)! I actually arrived a few minutes late due to a flight delay and they let me onto the next time slot! Very nice folks working at the Premium tours! They were very helpful and sympathetic towards traffic and flight delays. On the other hand, when I got to Victoria Rail Station, the signage could have been much better (especially as someone who doesn't know where they are going), and bus wifi was advertised on the website but was unavailable on the bus which was frustrating. Otherwise, the day was great, especially the fact that you can store luggage for free at the Studios! Very Helpful!

Absolutely brilliant. After 2 cancelled visits due to covid we made it today. Spent 3.5 hrs there, well worty it. My 12 year old son loved it. So much to see there, would go again.

Very interesting for fans and even people not really into Harry Potter too.

Plenty of parking that is free so don't fall for paying £10 parking at time of booking.

Butterbeer gorgeous reminded me of ice cream soda.

Visiting is definately a must.

Very well organised with the covid situation too.

Staff are all lovely, helpful and very informative.

The staff both the premium tour and the studio where nice. The bus stop location is very confusing where their no guide to it and it is closed to anther tour company location. When we arrived their was no sign that indicate the tour where the place also gather people going to the airport. Pulse the bus was a little bit late, so for people who value the time to explore the studio probably they should no that this lost time where not consider to be given for the return trip. Otherwise the studio it self was a fun trip and you can take your food, snakes and drinks with you.

Wasn’t sure what to expect when we arrived however we are highly delighted with a fabulous day out with the grandkids and family. The car park welcome stats the day well and every member of the cast or team we came into contact with throughout the day were so helpful and friendly you could ask for better. For Potter fans it’s an absolute treat. The pre show and cinema set you up for a fabulous day. You’d probably need to visit several times to see and experience everything on the tour. Plenty of free onsite parking and short queues at security when you check in. The drawback is the price of food and drink inside. There are a couple of places to eat and an amazing g gift shop. Large queue at the cafe halfway through the tour. The pièce de résistance is the tour itself no spoilers here just a bit of advice. Take your time, take video and photos, keep your eyes and ears open, experience everything you can and don’t miss a thing. Fabulous day out thank team HP Studios will definitely come back again.

Wow! What an amazing experience. We visited with our 7yr old daughter and we loved every minute of the studio tour. If you’re a Harry Potter fan then you’ll love this experience. So many props and scenes to explore - it took us about three hours.

For those with children, it was great to have toilets at points throughout the tour and the cafe half way through. Although on the expensive side, the food and treats were great. A butter beer is a must to try - we shared one between three of us which was enough. I wasn’t too keen on the taste but glad to have tried it!

The shop at the end of the experience was hard to walk through without making purchases! The personalised robe was excellent quality. It was certainly an expensive experience but worth every penny. Staff were fantastic, helpful and full of knowledge.

An amazing evening!

Although I am not a hardcore Harry Potter fan like my wife and son, I really enjoyed it. Seeing some of the sets and props used in all the films. I was surprised how much time and went into the transition from book to screen. Staff knew their stuff, and there was plenty of them about to answer any questions. Although with other plans we had that day it worked we had our tea's there and I wasn't keen. This was as I thought it wouldn't be value for money but I was pleasantly surprised. The cod and chips I had was a good size portion, and it tasted good too. Thought the butterbeer was pricey, but it was very nice. The tour took us almost 4hrs to get around, but it was very good. Due to my son wearing a green t-shirt, the additionally priced ride the broom video made him look like having an invisible torso, so check the website on what colour top to wear if you think you might do this experience. Unfortunately due to Covid-19, robes to wear to hide this dressing error were not available. A really pleasant, informative few hours getting up close to the set and props of the films.

I admit I have only seen 4 movies, and haven't read the books, but took my granddaughter as she is a big fan. It is very well done, and also interesting to those of us who are just accompanying our HP fans. Allow most of a day as there is so much to see, study and interact with. There's also a never-ending gift shop!

The trip was brilliant, until they managed to mess up our films of ridding brooms for my son and me. It is expensive to do this things, and it was a nightmare to get my son to do it in the first place. He was so proud when he did. And we never got the videos, tried to contact them about coming to retacke it before we left the UK. But ohh no, no problem this happens all the time. We always find them. The day after leaving UK they aperantly had a technical problem and could not retrieve them. We could get our money back, but that was not the point. This was supposed to give my son a bost, not bring him down more.

This is a really fantastic day out but not entirely suitable for people with a hearing impairment. Quite a few of the exhibits have screens with people talking and not one had subtitles. This excludes hearing impaired people from the tour. With the franchise being 20 years old, I'd have expected it back then, but in 2022 with the technology we have, this is unforgivable WB Tours.
Even on the shuttle bus provided there were only subtitles when Warwick Davis was speaking but no more.

You catch the bus outside of Watford station. It is £3 per person return. You don’t need the audio guide, there is so much information and guides to talk too as you go around. Lots of opportunities to take free photos and pay for additional ones. We had the butter beer but to be honest we only got it for the tankard, however I wish I had waited to buy the ones in the souvenir shop because they we better and more variety. Make sure you got walking shoes on and take your time. Tour is about 3 hours with a rest in between. The food is not great so bring a snack. Can sit outside or indoors to eat. Overall, an excellent family day out.

Wow!!! What an exciting experience! I cannot recommend this enough..
If you are a Harry Potter fan, or even if you’re not, you should still just visit for the experience.. such a wonderful day out, and an insight to how hard all the staff behind all these films work… I could go on, but I won’t spoil it for you….. go and see for yourself.. easy to get to from Watford Junction station, a bus will take you straight to the studio at £3 per person… bout 10 mins. Expect to be on there for 2-3 hours… totally worth it.🥳🤭🤗😍😍

Absolutely loved the studio tour! We went about mid day, it was busy but not too crowded. Staff were friendly and offered extra information whenever they could. Though I wouldn’t recommend the green screen photos as there are plenty of free photo opportunities around the studio. They even have a gluten free option for food.

As a Harry Potter fan this place was amazing, you saw all the costumes the original actors wore, from the first movie to the last. You see where everything is filmed, and there are loads of surprises on the tour too. All the staff are extremely friendly and they knew all the answers to all my questions.
This tour would take the whole day, if staying in london, it does take a while to get to the place with transport but it does lead you to the doors of the studio itself.
You get to try butter beer, which is so unique to any other drink i’ve tasted before.
You get to try out flying on brooms and taking your picture for askiban prison.
It was an amazing experience and the only thing I would suggest is to make sure you have the whole day for the trip because you don’t want to rush it.

Fantastic! A must go for any Harry Potter fan, its wonderful, the only thing I didn't like were all the people that were also there, the crowds were so big you didn't get anything to yourself and very hard to take nice photos. The shops throughout were very very expensive. TAKE YOUR OWN LUNCH! If your going for a long time. The sets and staff were all fantastic, it's a lovely experience.

I booked this for my husband and I as we'd loved the films - watched with our 2 boys (now grown up). Our 22 year old son has been more than once with his girlfriend so we thought we should give it a go. We were not disappointed even having been to the US and been on the Potter themed rides etc. Super well organised. SO interesting and, more importantly, magical - it's inspired us to watch the movies again. Great tour.

I have not even made it through one Harry Potter film, but the kids wanted to go and it was fabulous. You could take your time, soak up the sets and read in depth about the set design and details. Worth every penny really.

The Harry Potter Experience itself was great for any fan. This particular tour was rushed because the tour operator showed up late, we departed 45 minutes late. Then, we sat in the freezing cold when they were late to pick us up by 30 minutes.

Premiere tours made it easy for us to visit the studios by bus from central London. Good day out, smooth operation. Our time at the studio was our own (4 hours) and they provided the transport and the enterance ticket. Very good service

Really great tour. All very covid friendly and clean. Lots to see. Loads of photo opportunities. You can buy a personalised journal which is a great touch!!! The bank was stunning. The castle was superb. The dragon effect in the bank was amazing with fire and smoke. The gift shop had so many things too. Lots of little affordable gifts as well as big purchases. I loved platform 9 & 3/4 and being allowed on the train. Very well organised and all the attendants were very knowledgeable. Great day out for all.

This was our second visit and probably won’t be our last! The Forbidden Forrest and Gringotts have been added since our last visit and we really enjoyed these. There is so much to see and enjoy - you could easily spend 4 or 5 hours here. A must for any Harry Potter fan!

The Harry Potter tour is the best film tour I’ve visited! It’s well worth it. This tour gives you 4 hours which is plenty of time to get though everything! The departure point for this tour needs to be included to say which stance we are specifically supposed to meet at. We had to walk around the whole place asking for help on where to go. I messaged the tour company but by the time we received an answer we were already on the bus. I called also but no answer. Other than that, all was smooth!

Me and my girlfriend visited post lockdown. Unlike other places I have visited, Harry Potter studios was very well signposted and clean for covid safety.

The experience was unforgettable and something I would definitely do again.

The studio was everything we expected and more! Went with two Harry Potter fans (14 and 11 y) and they loved every second. We would have liked to have more time in the studio. When I return with my youngest one I would plan for a trip that gave us at least one more hour to enjoy.

We had a private tour due to my friend being partially sighted and having a guide dog. Andy was incredible. The studios are epic and massive, you can be there for hours! Andy showed us everything and explained everything. The sets are amazing and just stunning to view. If you can get a private tour do it. If not, and you’re a Harry Potter fan it’s a must see, this place has everything. Andy our tour guide had so much knowledge, was so helpful and just a lovely all round guy, he made our experience so wonderful. All staff were also so attentive, lovely and helpful. The studio is magical and I highly recommend it.

We went on this tour on May 24. Paola was our driver, and he is very entertaining. The tour is much more than we expected taking almost 5 hours to complete. My daughter had a blast . The Bank and the train are worth the trip, and there is so much more. I highly recommend this tour.

Amazing story & props to these fabulous films. You start with a group tour & short introduction & then are left to wander & explore.
Don’t bother with head phones unless you are on your own as an adult. There’s far too much to see & listen to without them.

It was amazing right from the entrance. There were people stationed around to help and answer questions. They would chat with the solo adventurer and would make you feel welcome. There were many green screen areas for the kids to get into the movie. They were all very joyful.

Giving this tour a thumbs up! Very comfortable with a coachride roundtrip, easy to find the bus stop at Victoria Coach Station. Just wish we had an extra hour, as 4 hours isn`t enough time at the attraction. When we thought we`d gone at least halfway through the tour, a guide told us that we were only 1/4 done. That meant rushing through the last 3/4 of it to make it to the coach back :-P

Ensure you leave enough time. We got stuck on the M25 and just got there. The shop was accessible at the beginning so we had a look round. I won't talk about the prices....but the range is phenomenal. The beginning of the tour feels like your cattle but it does open into the great hall. Which is a great entrance. Unfortunately given a time limit there so had to move on. Loads of photo opportunities. Loads and loads to look at. Particularly liked the forbidden forest spiders and the best was Diagon Alley. Just amazing and proves how much work is put in to produce such remarkable films. So much in the windows that you never see in the films. We were there four hours, but could have gone round again. Only downside why oh why does a big company charge for photos....?? Overall I hope we get time in our lifetime to go round again.

My daughter and I have been looking forward to this trip for months and it certainly didn’t disappoint, easily a good 4 hours to look all around and could stretch it out longer if you wanted to as there’s loads to see. The cafe is quite expensive but that’s to be expected in such places. Thoroughly good day out.

Had the most amazing day here! The attention to detail is stunning. The sets and costumes are magical and there are some fantastic surprises along the way.
All very COVID safe and lots of social distancing measures in place.
The staff are so friendly and knowledgable. Loved every moment just as much as my children. Definitely try the butter beer too- delicious!
Would definitely recommend and hope to revisit again in the future.

Fabulous tour we really enjoyed it. Comfortable coach and an amazing experience once we arrived. Blown away by the size of the sets and wow factors at every turn.
Finding the coach was tricky at Victoria Coach Station. We had to ask the information desk which was not manned until 5 minutes before our boarding time. Was expecting a Harry Potter decorated bus but was a normal coach which was fine.

If I could give this 100 stars I would. This was the best day out I've ever had.
As a Harry Potter fan this was amazing. Leave yourself plenty of time to go round. We were approx 3.5hrs and I feel as if I want to go back as I didn't take everything in.

From the minute you arrive you are in Harry Potter mode. Lots to see as you're waiting for your tour. Plenty of facilities and you can grab a coffee if you have to wait.

Staff fron the start to the end of the tour were amazing. Plenty of staff throughout who are more than happy to answer questions.

I cannot recommend this enough. I was with 2 non Harry Potter fans and they enjoyed the experience.

It's a must for all Potter fans. I will be booking to come back.

If you are a Harry Potter Fan and are ever in England this is a must see attraction. It took a short bus ride, but the 5 hours we spent wandering the entire place was well worth it!. The highlight for me was the miniature version of Hogwarts used for filming flybys!

I took the Grandchildren here who are massive fans of the film series. They were in awe of the fantastic sets and the whole experience. As someone who's never watched the films, I can say it is still a very enjoyable experience all in all. The level of detail is amazing. I would definitely recommend

This tour was AWESOME!! It was much more comprehensive than we expected. Sooooo many details and very interactive. Whether you are a die hard fan or not, this tour is super fun for the whole family. Very well organized, high production value, thoughtful and incredibly detailed. It is great that they have a cafeteria between the two stages - you will definitely want to stop there to refuel and enjoy the outdoor sets. I would definitely return a second time.

If you like Harry Potter you’ve got to come here. We’ve visited Harry Potter World in Orlando & this is a completely different yet exciting experience. The sets are amazing & the staff a very insightful & helpful.

Amazing! A must visit if you are a Harry Potter fan. Easy to find, plenty of parking, weren't long wait times. I would high recommend visiting, the different areas are very well laid out, plenty to see and experience. Lots of photo opportunities!

Just back for Harry Potter fans they will love it. I’m not particularly but it was still a good experience. I personally wouldn’t return for it’s it’s a one off visit but my daughter would go back quite a few times I would have thought and she’s 15
